name: l3_at1_handover
description: PR #447 (L3 + AT1): smooth sun/moon handover. Same scenario for the windows-latest 82080 baseline (the knobs below are then skipped as missing).

skies.label: PBR Default
skies.why: The viewer's default sky made PBR (reflection probe ambiance 1); the reference sky of doc/light/light-reference-numbers.md (row 2), sun 66 degrees at noon.

skies.label: PBR sunset, moon high
skies.why: Owner check 1/3: a sunset with the moon high in the sky (the swing and the moon's fade-in are the most visible here). Moon 55 degrees up, 90 degrees from the sun.

skies.label: PBR sunset, moon rising opposite
skies.why: Owner check 1: a warm creator sunset (Bangko 2 is in the owner's inventory; Bangko 1, the test's reddest low-sun sky, is the second candidate) with the moon rising opposite the sun, 12 degrees up.

skies.label: Classic Default
skies.why: Owner check 2: a classic sky (reflection probe ambiance 0, as every shipped sky): noon must match windows-latest, the low sun reddens, haze on fullbright objects.

skies.label: Phototools Yellow Stars 01
skies.why: Owner check: the sky with a negative distance multiplier (cloud sun 1.22 against the old formula); noon plus sweep. Skipped if the item is not in the inventory.

skies.label: No moon (moon brightness 0)
skies.why: Owner check 4: a sky with moon_brightness 0 has no direct light at night. Personal Lighting has no moon brightness slider, so this selects Default, opens the fixed sky editor (which starts from a clone of the current sky) and sets moon_brightness 0 there. Untested path; optional.
